title: Pushout of a short exact sequence along a morphism
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ be a short exact sequence in $\mathcal A$ and let $u:A\to I$ be any morphism. Let $E=I\amalg_AB$ be the pushout of $u$ and $f$ (it exists, being $\operatorname{Coker}((u,-f):A\to I\oplus B)$), with canonical morphisms $\iota:I\to E$ and $v:B\to E$, $\iota\circ u=v\circ f$. Then there is a unique morphism $p:E\to C$ with $p\circ v=g$ and $p\circ\iota=0$, and $0\to I\xrightarrow{\iota}E\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$ is a short exact sequence; thus $(u,v,\mathrm{id}_C)$ is a morphism from the first short exact sequence to the second.

source.place: Section Tag 010I (section-extensions, line 1260), item (2) after the definition of Ext (line 1349: the pushout E' = A' amalg_A E of an extension via A -> A', a commutative diagram of short exact sequences, 'by Lemma lemma-cartesian-cocartesian'); Lemma Tag 08N4 (lemma-cartesian-cocartesian) part (2) for the monomorphism, Lemma Tag 08N3 (lemma-cartesian-kernel) part (2) for the cokernel, Example Tag 05PJ (example-fibre-product-pushouts) for the pushout; used in derived.tex Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 1

proof.text: **Step 1 (the pushout exists).** By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](d) the abelian category $\mathcal A$ has pushouts: there are an object $E$ and morphisms $\iota:I\to E$, $v:B\to E$ with $\iota\circ u=v\circ f$ such that any $j':I\to W$, $k':B\to W$ with $j'\circ u=k'\circ f$ factor as $j'=\varphi\circ\iota$, $k'=\varphi\circ v$ for a unique $\varphi:E\to W$ (the pushout in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]).

source.place: Lemma Tag 010D (lemma-colimit-abelian-category: finite colimits exist) and Section Tag 010I (section-extensions), item (2) after the definition of Ext: E' = A' amalg_A E

proof.text: **Step 2 (the pushout as a cokernel).** Let $\pi:I\oplus B\to Q$ be a cokernel of $(u,-f):A\to I\oplus B$ (biproducts and cokernels exist in $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-abelian]), and let $\iota_Q=\pi\circ\mathrm{in}_I$, $v_Q=\pi\circ\mathrm{in}_B$. Morphisms $\psi:I\oplus B\to W$ correspond bijectively to pairs $(j',k')=(\psi\,\mathrm{in}_I,\psi\,\mathrm{in}_B)$, and $\psi\circ(u,-f)=j'u-k'f$; so pairs with $j'u=k'f$ are exactly the $\psi$ killing $(u,-f)$, and these factor uniquely through $\pi$. Hence $(Q,\iota_Q,v_Q)$ is a pushout of $u$ and $f$, and $E\cong\operatorname{Coker}((u,-f))$ compatibly with $\iota$, $v$ (uniqueness of colimits up to unique isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]). This identification is the parenthetical claim of the statement and is not used below.

**Step 3 (the morphism $p$).** Since the first sequence is a complex, $g\circ f=0=0\circ u$; so the pair $j'=0:I\to C$, $k'=g:B\to C$ satisfies $j'u=k'f$, and by the universal property of Step 1 there is a unique $p:E\to C$ with $p\circ\iota=0$ and $p\circ v=g$. This is the existence and uniqueness of $p$ claimed.

source.place: Section Tag 010I (section-extensions), item (2): the commutative diagram of short exact sequences with right vertical map id_B

proof.text: **Step 4 ($\iota$ is a monomorphism).** $f:A\to B$ is a monomorphism (the sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ is short exact) and $(E,\iota,v)$ is the pushout of $f$ and $u$; by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-pushout-mono] applied with $a=f:G=A\to G'=B$, $b=u:A\to F=I$, the canonical map $a'=\iota:I\to E$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 08N4 (lemma-cartesian-cocartesian, line 887), part (2), with g := f monic and h := iota; also Lemma Tag 05PK (lemma-epimorphism-universal-abelian-category), part (2)

proof.text: **Step 5 ($p$ is a cokernel of $\iota$).** The square with $w=A$, $y=B$, $x=I$, $z=E$, top $f:A\to B$, left $u:A\to I$, right $v:B\to E$, bottom $\iota:I\to E$ commutes ($v f=\iota u$) and is cocartesian (Step 1). Since $0\to A\xrightarrow fB\xrightarrow gC\to0$ is short exact, $g$ is a cokernel of $f$ [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](a) ($g$ is an epimorphism and the sequence is exact at $B$). Let $c:E\to K$ be a cokernel of $\iota$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-cokernel-iso] (with $\pi_f=g$, $\pi_k=c$, $h=v$, $k=\iota$) the morphism $\theta:C\to K$ with $\theta\circ g=c\circ v$ is an isomorphism. Put $p'=\theta^{-1}\circ c:E\to C$. Then $p'\circ\iota=0$ and $p'\circ v=\theta^{-1}\theta g=g$, so $p'=p$ by the uniqueness in Step 3. Thus $p$ is the composite of the cokernel $c$ of $\iota$ with an isomorphism, hence itself a cokernel of $\iota$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 08N3 (lemma-cartesian-kernel, line 852), part (2): Coker(f) -> Coker(k) induced by h is an isomorphism for a cocartesian square

proof.text: **Step 6 (conclusion).** $\iota$ is a monomorphism (Step 4) and $p$ is a cokernel of $\iota$ (Step 5), so $0\to I\xrightarrow{\iota}E\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$ is a short exact sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](c). The squares $\iota\circ u=v\circ f$ (Step 1) and $p\circ v=g=\mathrm{id}_C\circ g$ (Step 3) commute, so $(u,v,\mathrm{id}_C)$ is a morphism of short exact sequences.

lean.statement: theorem pushout_short_exact_sequence {𝒜 : Type u} [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Abelian 𝒜] (S : ShortComplex 𝒜) (hS : S.ShortExact) {I : 𝒜} (u : S.X₁ ⟶ I) : (∃ e : pushout u S.f ≅ cokernel (biprod.lift u (-S.f)), pushout.inl u S.f ≫ e.hom = biprod.inl ≫ cokernel.π (biprod.lift u (-S.f)) ∧ pushout.inr u S.f ≫ e.hom = biprod.inr ≫ cokernel.π (biprod.lift u (-S.f))) ∧ ∃ p : pushout u S.f ⟶ S.X₃, ∃ hz : pushout.inl u S.f ≫ p = 0, pushout.inr u S.f ≫ p = S.g ∧ (∀ q : pushout u S.f ⟶ S.X₃, pushout.inr u S.f ≫ q = S.g → pushout.inl u S.f ≫ q = 0 → q = p) ∧ (ShortComplex.mk (pushout.inl u S.f) p hz).ShortExact ∧ ∃ m : S ⟶ ShortComplex.mk (pushout.inl u S.f) p hz, m.τ₁ = u ∧ m.τ₂ = pushout.inr u S.f ∧ m.τ₃ = 𝟙 S.X₃
